title: ISic002238. Fragmentary Greek funerary inscription
body:
Text encoding: Jonathan Prag; edition source: autopsy Prag 2026-09-17, archaeological park of Neapolis
1Μοσ̣[.. 19.5 cm ..]
2Εὐπολεμ̣[.. 11 cm ..]

Text encoding: Jonathan Prag; edition source: autopsy Prag 2026-09-17, archaeological park of Neapolis
1ΜΟ.[.. 19.5 cm ..]
2ΕΥΠΟΛΕ.[.. 11 cm ..]

Facsimile Images

Apparatus criticus

  • Text from autopsy ;
  • 1: Orsi: Μο[σ...]; 11 cm are missing from the right side at this point
  • 2: Orsi: Εὐπολέ[μου]; 19.5cm are missing from the right side at this point

English translation

Jonathan Prag

Mos[--] son of Eupolem[--]

commentary

Traces of the sigma and mu at the breaks are visible. Given the missing space (18 cm up to the sigma trace, c.19.5 cm missing), not more than three letters can be missing from line 1, so Μόσχος (attested at Syracuse and Akragas and Tauromenion) seems very likely, or just possibly Μοσχίων. In line 2, given the missing space of c.11cm (26.5 preserved), only 2-3 letters can be missing, and so Orsi's suggestion of Εὐπόλεμος (attested at Syracuse and multiple other Sicilian locations in the Hellenistic period) is surely correct.

bibliography

  • Orsi NSA 1907 751 with fig. 10 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10001392

Elegant thinly carved letters. The trace of sigma on line 1 suggests a rather open four-bar sigma; Epsilon has short middle bar; Pi has short right hand hasta; omicron is sligthly smaller than other letters; Mu has vertical outer strokes, half-length inner strokes.

Line 1 42-50 Line 2 30-42 Interlineation line 1 to 2
